staticText: Local-first English–Yoruba phrasebook with 175 embedded starter records, tone-marked core fixtures, ten ambiguity-sensitive usage notes, and a local orthography lab. The app-local draft is not fully tone-marked or speaker-signed-off. Optional uncached cloud machine translation requires explicit, non-persistent page-session consent.
boundaries: Preserve tone marks, dot-below letters, apostrophes, spelling, and punctuation exactly where supplied; never flatten Báwo ni, Ẹ káàárọ̀, Ẹ ṣéun, Iṣẹ́, Ikọ́, or Ẹ̀jẹ̀ ríru into plain-keyboard text.
Tone marking is incomplete across the inventory; do not claim exhaustive orthography, dialect coverage, or human-quality translation.
Keep owó, ọwọ́, and ọ̀wọ̀ distinct; keep ilé and ilẹ̀ distinct; explain oko and ogun ambiguity instead of guessing from unmarked text.
Nigerian, Beninese, Togolese, community, and diaspora usage can vary. Important wording requires qualified human review.
Never place raw source or translated text in storage, URLs, analytics, accounts, email, logs, or caches.
